text:
The estate can most likely recover damages for the wound and for the pain and suffering up to the point she refused the transfusion. It probably can't recover for her death, because her refusal of the treatment that would have saved her is treated as cutting off the driver's liability for that later harm. Contributory negligence doesn't bar the whole claim, since the driver's negligence still caused the original injury. I'm not fully sure of this: under the eggshell-plaintiff rule, many courts would let the estate recover for the death too, which is what I said earlier. I'm choosing from the two options in the team note, and this is the better fit of those two.

CONFIDENCE: 55
